children: Shares of luxury electric car manufacturer Lucid
jumped 6.8% in the afternoon session after the company announced a strategic partnership with European shared mobility platform Bolt to develop and deploy autonomous mobility services across Europe.

Under the agreement, Bolt aims to deploy at least 25,000 autonomous Lucid vehicles built on Lucid's upcoming Midsize platform and powered by NVIDIA Hyperion. The companies stated they will collaborate starting from the product-development phase on an SAE Level 4 autonomous driving system-ready vehicle platform. SAE Level 4 systems enable vehicles to handle all driving functions under designated conditions without human driver intervention. The initiative represents a major step toward Bolt's goal of introducing 100,000 autonomous vehicles onto its European platform by 2035.
The shares closed the day at $4.30, up 7.1% from the previous close.
What Is The Market Telling Us

Lucid’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 67 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 24 days ago when the stock dropped 5.9% on the news that trade negotiations between the United States and Canada broke down, sparking concerns over new 50% tariffs and retaliatory trade measures. Bilateral trade negotiations between Washington and Ottawa collapsed unexpectedly, triggering the implementation of 50% tariffs on approximately $20 billion worth of Canadian imports, including electrical equipment and building materials.

Lucid is down 61.5% since the beginning of the year, and at $4.30 per share, it is trading 82.7% below its 52-week high of $24.77 from October 2025. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Lucid’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $18.71.
